title: MapleStory Classic Fighter Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 30-70
intro: Fighters are MapleStory's front-line brawlers. They train under Dances with Balrog, carry swords or axes, and do their best work by face tanking everything, getting up close and personal with mobs.

blocks.p: This guide is based off of a realistic lv 70 Fighter build by Grummash.
**Pros**

ul: #1 Damage/MP at level 70: very mana efficient when it comes to dealing damage.
Max Rage gives nearby party members +40 Attack Power and -40 WDEF; decent boost to physical damage.
Huge variety of weapon options: 1H sword/axe and 2H sword/axe.

blocks.p: **Cons**

ul: Short reach and limited mobility; constantly face tanking.
Weapon Mastery, Booster, and Final Attack lock SP to one weapon path.
Power Strike and Slash Blast remain the main DPS skills until level 70+ third job.

blocks.h2: Levels 30-70: Fighter skill build and leveling

blocks.p: The default order takes Rush at level 30 and Rage at level 31, unlocks Booster and Final Attack, maxes Mastery, then finishes Rage, Final Attack, Booster, and Rush. It considers party value, minimum damage, MP upkeep, and mobility.

ol: Talk to Dances with Balrog in Perion and start **The Warrior's Next Journey**.
Take his letter to the Warrior Job Instructor in West Rocky Mountain IV.
Enter the test, defeat the monsters, and collect 30 Dark Marbles.
Return with **The Proof of a Hero** and choose **Fighter**.

blocks.note: **Power Guard is a third-job skill in Classic World.** Fighter gets Rush during second job. Power Guard appears in the Crusader skill book.

blocks.p: Grummash's realistic level 70 two-handed axe Fighter is the reference build for the main SP order. Sword Fighters use Sword Mastery, Final Attack: Sword, and Sword Booster at the same levels as the matching axe skills.

blocks.note: **Rush arrives immediately:** Rush 1 moves the Fighter forward, pushes up to four mobs, prevents knockback during the movement, and costs 40 MP.

blocks.p: Second-job SP cannot be spent on first-job skills, so finish the first-job plan by level 30. Character Builder flags any build that breaks it.

blocks.h3: Possible changes to the default order

blocks.p: Booster 1 already gives +2 Attack Speed stages. Taking it to 10 after Mastery 20 reduces upkeep and recasting. This is the best QoL change when MP is tight.
Rush 10 increases its distance by a bit and costs 31 MP. Add SP here when grouping or crossing the map saves more time than another point in a damage skill.

blocks.cap: Sword Booster: faster sword attacks after five points in Sword Mastery.
Axe Booster: faster axe attacks after five points in Axe Mastery.
Rush: movement, grouping, and protection from knockback during the dash.

blocks.note: **Simple grinding loop:** Max Rage and Booster both last 300 seconds, so refresh them together. Leave Final Attack toggled on when its three-target follow-up improves your clear speed, use Rush to group the mobs, then Power Strike one target or Slash Blast several.

blocks.p: Ducky Duck Gaming's Fighter overview also walks through this buff cycle and the Final Attack toggle.
The table is a sample path. Keep total DEX at the minimum your next weapon needs, subtract DEX supplied by other gear, and put the rest into STR.
This sample spends 3 STR and 2 DEX per level from 31 through 36, then returns to 4 STR and 1 DEX through level 57. At level 57, base DEX reaches 60. Every AP from level 58 through 70 goes into STR.

Rage raises Attack Power for nearby party members and lowers WDEF. Attack Power is used by physical attacks. Magic spells use Magic Attack, so Rage does not affect their spell damage.
The party area grows at lv 16. See the level 1 and level 30 diagrams below.

blocks.h3: How Attack Power affects Warrior damage

blocks.note:
**Raw physical damage**
MAX = (1 + (STR x Weapon Multiplier + DEX) / 100 + Attack Power / 50) x W.ATK x Skill Power
MIN = (0.8 + (STR x Weapon Multiplier x Mastery + DEX) / 100 + Attack Power / 50) x W.ATK x Skill Power
Mastery = (Mastery Level / 10 + 0.1) x 0.8

blocks.p: **Rage boosts both the MIN and MAX damage range.**

blocks.h3: Max Rage on a Lv 70 Fighter's Power Strike

blocks.p: Grummash's fighter build has 337 STR, 70 DEX, 105 W.ATK, max Axe Mastery, and a max 260% Power Strike. Against an equal-level target with 0 WDEF:
**For this build, max Rage boosts average Power Strike damage by about 8.1%.**

In this formula, +40 Attack Power contributes the same raw damage term as +80 DEX. On a two-handed axe it takes roughly 27-45 STR to match that term, depending on the attack action and whether the roll uses Mastery. Rage is indeed a meaningful physical damage buff.

blocks.cap: Rage: skill Lv16 is the party-range breakpoint; skill Lv30 gives +40 Attack Power for five minutes.

blocks.p: Final Attack is a toggle. At max, it has a 50% chance to add a 140% follow-up against up to three mobs after an attack skill. It shows no extra HP or MP cost.
Page and Spearman Final Attacks hit one target. Fighter's three-target follow-up is the better fit for grouped grinding, especially after Slash Blast leaves several mobs alive.

Each FA proc has its own attack animation after your skill finishes, and you can't attack again until it ends: about 0.6 seconds with Booster. Fighter's Final Attack: Sword and Final Attack: Axe spread to up to three mobs, so you do more damage overall against two or three mobs. Against one mob it doesn't and is better to toggle FA off.
Keep it on for small groups. Turn it off for bosses and single mob farming.
Final Attack costs no MP, so it also saves potions: about 26% more damage per MP against one mob and 39% against four. Keep it on when MP is your limit, even against groups.

blocks.cap: Final Attack: Axe: 50% chance, 140% damage, and up to three mobs at skill Lv30.

blocks.p: One-handed Fighters attack faster and can equip a shield. Two-handed Fighters get higher W.ATK, slightly longer attack range, and stronger weapon multipliers. Sword and axe both work; the choice changes your Mastery, Booster, and Final Attack skill path.

Same level 30 Fighter: 138 STR, 30 DEX, max Power Strike, Rush 1, Jousting Helmet, Steel Missel, and unscrolled weapons. Rage, Mastery, and Booster are still at 0. Damage uses a 0 WDEF target so the weapon difference is easy to compare.

Same level 70 stats as Grummash's build: 337 STR, 70 DEX, max Rage, max Mastery, max Booster, 14% Critical Rate, and +26% Critical Damage. Every weapon has seven successful Lesser Attack scrolls and the gloves add 5 W.ATK. Damage again uses a 0 WDEF target.

The shield can fully block eligible regular physical hits. Red Cross Shield has 110 WDEF, seven slots, and 18.0% Guard chance before scrolling. Gold Ancient Shield has 192 WDEF, +35 HP, seven slots, and 27.7% Guard chance before scrolling. Shield WDEF also lowers the hits that get through. Magic attacks cannot trigger Shield Guard, and some special attacks can bypass it.
Higher W.ATK and stronger damage multipliers win the Power Strike comparison at both levels. The higher minimum damage also makes guaranteed one-shot and two-shot kills easier to reach.
Shield DEF Scroll: Lesser has a 100% success rate and adds 2 WDEF per slot. The extra WDEF also raises Guard chance.

**Use Shield DEF Scroll: Lesser.** At level 70, seven Shield Accuracy Scrolls: Lesser add +7 ACC, but the realistic one-handed Fighter build gains no new 100%-hit mob, one- or two-hit map, or better Training Advisor map.

blocks.h3: Swords vs. axes: which is best?

blocks.p: **Axe deals more average damage.** At level 30, the one-handed axe is about 3.5% ahead of the one-handed sword, and the two-handed axe is about 4.5% ahead of the two-handed sword over one minute. At level 70, those gaps are about 4.7% and 3.1%. These numbers do not include Axe Mastery's bleed, which adds another chance for damage at max skill level.

**Sword gives steadier damage.** Swords use the same multiplier on swing and stab actions, so their minimum and maximum hits stay closer together. This helps when even the sword's weakest hit can guarantee a one-shot or two-shot kill. Sword Mastery also gives +90 WDEF.

Pick axe for higher average damage and bleed. Pick sword for more consistent damage rolls and extra WDEF. After choosing the weapon family, decide whether you want a shield or the higher damage of a two-handed weapon.

blocks.cap: One-handed sword: fast attacks, shield access, and a fixed 1.8 multiplier.
Two-handed axe: slower attacks with the highest Fighter swing multiplier.

blocks.p: Every melee hit lands inside a box in front of you, called the hitbox. Its length is your weapon's reach. A sword or axe has five basic attacks, three swings and two thrusts, with a box for each. Each attack uses one of the five at random. The strips list the average reach of one basic attack for the level 30-70 weapons.

blocks.cap: Scimitar, Swing 1. Any monster whose body touches the blue box gets hit: 47-100 px in front of you, from 2 px below your feet to 95 px above them.

blocks.p: Some two-handed weapons reach farther. Scimitar, Lion's Fang, Sparta, and Doombringer average 102 px per basic attack. Two-handed axes and the other two-handed swords average 87-90 px, while one-handed swords and axes average 74-86 px. Reach has a direct effect on DPS in practice. Longer reach makes mobs easier to hit from a distance and keeps them from getting close enough to hit you. Our weapon reach guide charts every weapon family.

blocks.h2: W.ATK or Critical Rate on gloves?

blocks.p: These numbers use Grummash's realistic level 70 Fighter build and five successful Lesser glove scrolls. Both options use the same five slots.

**+5 W.ATK**
100 to 105 total W.ATK
About 5% more expected damage.

**+5% Critical Rate**
14% to 19% Critical Rate
About 1.25% more expected damage.

blocks.note: **Pick Attack.** The five-scroll Attack setup deals about 3.7% more expected damage than the Critical Rate setup on this build.

blocks.p: Fighter has only 26% Critical Damage in this build. Critical Rate does not gain enough per point to challenge W.ATK.

**The ratio is the same at every grade.** Lesser gives +1 W.ATK or +1% Critical Rate (+2 M.ATK), Intermediate +2/+2% (+4 M.ATK), Greater +3/+3% (+6 M.ATK), and Chaos +4/+4% (+8 M.ATK). Matching grades have the same success and destruction rates.

**W.ATK also helps guaranteed kills.** It raises every physical hit, including your weakest normal roll and every critical hit. Critical Rate changes how often a critical occurs, so it cannot improve the weakest non-critical roll.

blocks.h2: Find Your Build's Best Training Map with Training Advisor

blocks.p: **Danger measures how hard a mob hits you for: under 10% of your HP is Safe, 10-24% is Caution, 25-49% is Danger, and 50%+ is Lethal.**
The example builds above use Power Strike with Final Attack off. Their picks include only 100% hit targets that the minimum damage roll kills in one or two hits, ranked by EXP per required hit.

blocks.note:
**Guaranteed Power Strike kills**
Guaranteed 1-shot: Min / hit >= Mob HP
Guaranteed 2-shot: 2 x Min / hit >= Mob HP
**Min / hit is your weakest possible hit.** If that number is at least the mob's HP, every Power Strike kills it in one hit. A guarantee also requires 100% hit rate because a miss deals no damage.

ol: Open your saved build in Character Builder and enter your real level, AP, equipment, scrolls, skill levels, HP, MP, WDEF, and MDEF.
Choose **Power Strike**. Enable Rage only when you expect to keep it active while training.
Open **By mob** and enable **Show min damage per hit**. Check Hit Rate, Min / hit, Hits / kill, and MP / kill.
Open **By map** and compare EXP, Danger, and the walk to the nearest potion shop.

blocks.p: Temporary potion and buff scenarios change the calculation without changing the saved build. This makes it easy to compare no buff, Rage, Accuracy potion, and Attack Power potion results.

blocks.note: **Level 70 cost example:** Grummash's Chrono build uses about 83 Power Strikes per minute. At 12 MP each, that is 996 MP, or 6.6 Lemons and 996 mesos per minute before Rage, Booster, Rush, HP food, or misses.

blocks.p: Accuracy potions pay for themselves when they remove misses or unlock a faster map. Test the potion in Training Advisor first. If your hit rate stays at 100% without it, spend the mesos elsewhere.
Most bad Fighter builds come from locking in weapon SP too early, forcing maps the character cannot hit, or spending mesos faster than the build earns them.

ol: **Spending Mastery SP before choosing sword or axe.** One-handed and two-handed weapons share the same family skills. Sword and axe do not.
**Moving to a higher-level map with poor hit rate.** A miss still consumes the attack's HP and MP. Check 100% hit and how many of your weakest hits are needed to kill first.
**Maxing Rush early.** Rush 1 is useful, but it costs 40 MP. Early skill levels can empty your MP bar and meso wallet.
**Leaving Final Attack on without testing it.** It helps when the follow-up finishes mobs and wastes time when Power Strike already guarantees the kill.

**Treating a shield as plain WDEF.** A shield can Guard and fully block eligible physical hits. Clean Guard chance is 18.0% on Red Cross Shield and 27.7% on Gold Ancient Shield. Shield DEF scrolls raise WDEF and Guard chance.
**Assuming Rage buffs magic.** Rage raises Attack Power used by physical attacks. It does not raise Magic Attack.
**Buying every armor upgrade while short on potions.** A weapon or Accuracy breakpoint matters more than a small WDEF increase. Keep enough mesos for HP food and Lemons.
